userStories.notes: Tier: quick-win. userStories.title: Optimize checkpoint backup rotation to skip on minor updates
acceptanceCriteria: Add a `min_rotation_interval_seconds` field (default 60) to checkpoint config in `src/config/sections/` and `config.yaml`
Modify `CheckpointManager._atomic_save()` in `src/checkpoint.py` to only rotate backups when elapsed time since last rotation exceeds the configured interval OR when a major stage completes
Add a `_last_rotation_time` timestamp tracking field to `CheckpointManager`
Add a test that verifies rapid successive saves do NOT trigger backup rotation when interval hasn't elapsed
Add a test that verifies backup rotation IS triggered when a stage boundary is crossed regardless of interval
Run `pytest tests/test_checkpoint*.py -v --tb=short -x` with no new failures
userStories.notes: Tier: targeted. Files: `src/checkpoint.py` (lines ~743-807, `_atomic_save` and backup rotation logic), `src/config/sections/core.py` or relevant config section. Currently rotates backups on EVERY save including minor stat updates during DOWNLOAD_SEGMENTS, which creates unnecessary I/O. Stage-boundary saves should always rotate; intermediate saves should respect the interval.

userStories.title: Add within-stage resumption support for MATCH stage
acceptanceCriteria: Add an `intermediate_checkpoint()` method call inside the MATCH stage's segment-processing loop (in `src/stages/match.py`) that saves progress every N segments (configurable, default 25)
Store partial match results in checkpoint under a `partial_matches` key so that on resume, already-matched segments are skipped
Add a `_restore_partial_matches()` method that loads partial results from checkpoint and merges with new results on completion
Add a test that simulates a MATCH stage interruption mid-way and verifies resumption starts from the last checkpointed segment, not from scratch
Add a test that verifies the final match results are identical whether run to completion or interrupted+resumed
Run `pytest tests/test_match*.py tests/test_checkpoint*.py -v --tb=short -x` with no new failures
userStories.notes: Tier: deep. Files: `src/stages/match.py` (lines ~683-779, `_run_matching`), `src/checkpoint.py` (CheckpointManager). Currently only DOWNLOAD_SEGMENTS has within-stage resumption. For large projects with 100+ voiceover segments, MATCH can take 10+ minutes and losing all progress on interruption wastes significant compute. The checkpoint already supports arbitrary keys via `save_stage_data()`.

userStories.title: Add config schema validation that fails fast on invalid YAML before pipeline runs
acceptanceCriteria: Create a `validate_config_schema()` function in `src/config/` that checks all required fields exist and have correct types before pipeline execution
Validate at minimum: all section names are recognized, numeric fields are numbers, boolean fields are booleans, nested objects match expected structure
Call `validate_config_schema()` early in pipeline initialization (before stage construction) in `src/pipeline.py`
Add a test with a config containing an unknown section name that triggers a warning (not error, for forward compat)
Add a test with a config containing a string where a number is expected that raises `ConfigValidationError`
Run `pytest tests/test_config*.py tests/test_pipeline*.py -v --tb=short -x` with no new failures
userStories.notes: Tier: targeted. Files: `src/config/` (new function or module), `src/pipeline.py` (line ~694, near `config.freeze()`). Currently config is only validated at runtime when individual fields are accessed, leading to cryptic errors deep in pipeline stages. Fail-fast on invalid YAML catches typos and structure issues before any work is done. Use `dataclasses.fields()` to auto-derive expected schema from config section dataclasses.

Add a `_format_log_context()` method to PipelineOrchestrator that returns a structured dict for inclusion in log messages

Run `pytest tests/test_pipeline*.py -v --tb=short -x` with no new failures
userStories.notes: Tier: targeted. Files: `src/pipeline.py` (logging calls at lines ~468-516 timing, ~559-597 quality gate, ~842 stage failure). userStories.title: Add randomized jitter to download adaptive delay to prevent thundering herd
acceptanceCriteria: Modify the adaptive delay calculation in `src/stages/download_segments.py` to add random jitter of +/-25% to the computed delay
Add a `jitter_factor` config field (default 0.25) in the download config section
Ensure jitter is applied consistently in both the main download loop and the retry queue processing
Add a test that runs the delay calculation 100 times and verifies the results are not identical (proving jitter is applied)
Add a test that verifies jitter stays within the configured bounds (delay * (1 - jitter_factor) to delay * (1 + jitter_factor))
Run `pytest tests/test_download*.py -v --tb=short -x` with no new failures
userStories.notes: Tier: quick-win. Files: `src/stages/download_segments.py` (lines ~752-754, ~833-837 adaptive delay logic), `src/config/sections/download.py`. Currently uses exponential backoff with a max cap but no randomization. When multiple segments hit rate limits simultaneously, they all retry at the exact same intervals, creating synchronized request bursts. Use `random.uniform(1 - jitter, 1 + jitter)` multiplier.

userStories.title: Build segment path index for O(1) file lookup in OUTPUT stage
acceptanceCriteria: Create a `SegmentPathIndex` class in `src/stages/output.py` (or new `src/segment_index.py`) that builds a dict mapping `(video_id, start, end)` tuples to file paths
Populate the index once at OUTPUT stage start by scanning both legacy `*_segments` dirs and flat download dir
Replace the per-match file discovery calls in `_scan_video_segments()` with index lookups
Add a test that verifies index lookup returns the correct path for a known segment file
Add a test that verifies index handles the case where a segment exists in both legacy and flat directories (flat dir takes precedence)
Run `pytest tests/test_pipeline*.py -v --tb=short -x` with no new failures
userStories.notes: Tier: targeted. Files: `src/stages/output.py` (lines ~112-214, `_scan_video_segments`). Currently scans directories for every match resolution, which is O(n*m) for n matches and m files. An upfront index scan is O(m) build + O(1) per lookup. Per CLAUDE.md rule 38, must check BOTH legacy dirs AND flat dir. Use `pathlib.Path.glob()` for initial scan.

userStories.title: Add partial success handling for parallel stage execution in pipeline orchestrator
acceptanceCriteria: Modify `_run_parallel_stages()` in `src/pipeline.py` to classify stages as `critical` (failure aborts) vs `optional` (failure logs warning but pipeline continues)
Add a `critical` boolean field (default True) to the stage registration metadata in `src/stages/__init__.py`
When an optional parallel stage fails, collect its error into a `partial_failures` list on PipelineState and continue with remaining stages
Add a test that runs two parallel stages where the optional one fails and verifies the pipeline completes with a warning
Add a test that runs two parallel stages where the critical one fails and verifies the pipeline aborts
Run `pytest tests/test_pipeline*.py -v --tb=short -x` with no new failures
userStories.notes: Tier: deep. Files: `src/pipeline.py` (lines ~974-1096, `_run_parallel_stages`), `src/stages/__init__.py` (stage registry decorator). Currently all parallel futures are collected before checking failures -- one failure cascades to abort all. For future parallel configurations (e.g., CAPTION + VIDEO_SEARCH in parallel), a failed optional stage shouldn't block the pipeline. Use `concurrent.futures.as_completed()` for early failure detection.
